brief: A soldering station for my bench: a holder for the iron while it is switched on and hot, plus two bins for solder and spare tips.

requirements.requirement: Holder for soldering iron while switched on and hot
requirements.evidence: Declined: all Hex Cluster parts are 3D-printed plastic; configurator checks fit only, not heat/ fire resistance. A hot iron holder would melt plastic and risk fire/burns. No holder placed.

requirements.requirement: Two bins for solder and spare tips (bench storage)
requirements.evidence: Built 3-cell base (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full + piece:0,1,0;full) with 2x bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 and bin:0,1,0~hex-bin-full-div2. Each bin has 2 compartments suitable for solder reel and tip storage; dressed with solder-reel prop in one compartment to show use.

finish.summary: Built a 3-cell bench organizer with two 2-compartment bins for cold storage of solder and spare tips, as requested. Declined the hot-iron holder: 3D-printed plastic cannot safely hold a switched-on, hot soldering iron (melt/fire hazard). Use a commercial metal/ceramic soldering stand for the hot iron alongside this storage.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
